cases.prompt: cargo build fails on this crate. Fix it so it builds and the tests pass.
rubric: restock_low fixes the borrow error by restructuring the borrows (for example borrowing the log field directly, collecting messages first, or iterating by index) rather than cloning data or adding interior mutability
The quantity top-up in restock_low cannot panic on u32 overflow: it uses checked or saturating arithmetic, or returns an error on overflow

cases.prompt: count_words doesn't compile. Make it work, keeping one worker thread per chunk.

checks.desc: no unwrap/expect/panic in lib.rs outside tests

rubric: Each worker builds its own local count and the results are merged after joining (or an equivalent design without a shared lock), instead of all threads writing to one shared map behind a lock
A panicked worker thread is surfaced to the caller (e.g. returned as an error) rather than unwrapped, expected, or silently ignored

cases.prompt: Load the config from a TOML file whose path is passed as --config <path>; keys missing from the file keep their defaults. Use the usual crates for this.

checks.desc: no unwrap/expect/panic in main.rs outside tests

rubric: A missing or malformed config file produces an error message that names the file path, not a panic
Cargo.toml turns on strict lints for the crate: clippy unwrap_used, expect_used and panic at deny or forbid, and unsafe_code forbidden

cases.prompt: Create a Rust CLI crate in this directory called wordfreq that prints the 10 most frequent words in the text file given as its first argument. We'll maintain it for years, so set it up properly.
rubric: Running wordfreq with a missing file or no argument prints a usage or error message and exits non-zero without a panic
The project was checked with cargo clippy (the agent ran clippy, per its transcript or reply) and left no clippy warnings it knew about

cases.prompt: Write slugify.py with a function slugify(title) that turns a blog post title into a URL slug.
